title: XIX. Kingly munus: titles and pertaining acts
pass_a_gloss: Pass A clause gloss (reordered): The means by which ye kingly munus stands as administered in ye church stand as chiefly ye Word and ye efficacy belonging toward ye Holy Spirit, which ought by no means to be separated out from each other. — (4) ye final judgment. — (3) defense against enemies; — (2) its governance by Word and Spirit; — To ye kingly munus pertain (1) ye calling and gathering belonging toward ye church; — XIX. — 2 Timothy 4:8). — Revelation 17:14), prince belonging toward ye kings belonging toward ye earth (Revelation 1:5), prince belonging toward peace (Isaiah 9:6), leader (Matthew 2:6), ruler (Micah 5:2), and judge (Acts 10:42; — Christ stands as king (Zechariah 9:9; — It stands as called kingly because it properly belongs to a king to govern, judge, and defend his people. — Latin anchors: Dicitur, autem, regium, regis, proprie, gubernare, iudicare, defendere, populum, Christus, princeps, regum, terrae, princeps, pacis, Matth, dominator, iudex, regium, munus
pass_b_english: It is called kingly because it properly belongs to a king to govern, judge, and defend his people. Christ is king (Zechariah 9:9; Revelation 17:14), prince of the kings of the earth (Revelation 1:5), prince of peace (Isaiah 9:6), leader (Matthew 2:6), ruler (Micah 5:2), and judge (Acts 10:42; 2 Timothy 4:8).

XIX. To the kingly munus pertain (1) the calling and gathering of the church; (2) its governance by Word and Spirit; (3) defense against enemies; (4) the final judgment. The means by which the kingly munus is administered in the church are chiefly the Word and the efficacy of the Holy Spirit, which ought by no means to be separated from each other.
source_text: Dicitur autem regium, quia regis proprie est gubernare, iudicare & defendere populum suum. Christus est rex, Zach. 9:9; Apoc. 17:14; princeps regum terrae, Apoc. 1:5; princeps pacis, Esa. 9:6; dux, Matth. 2:6; dominator, Mich. 5:2; iudex, Act. 10:42; 2 Tim. 4:8. XIX. Ad regium munus pertinent 1. vocatio & collectio ecclesiae; 2. gubernatio eius per verbum & Spiritum; 3. defensio contra hostes; 4. iudicium finale. Media, quibus regium munus administratur in ecclesia, potissimum sunt verbum & efficacia Spiritus S., quae a se invicem separari haud debent.
